page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. Multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and database operations fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average write speeds for large blocks and average read speeds for small cached blocks, though read-only bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weak, falling in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is poor, but text generation for small 135M models is strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16as_v6 offers high memory density relative to its compute footprint, allowing organizations to run memory-intensive applications without provisioning unnecessary CPU cores. This resource profile makes the instance well-suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, data compilation, and medium-scale web serving.
